prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” roofer for hurricane‑rated replacements — the right contractor depends on your house, budget, materials, and whether you need insurance‑claim help. Instead of one name, I can help you find the best local company by telling you exactly what to look for and how to vet candidates.

Key qualifications and credentials
- Miami‑Dade County Product Control/NOA familiarity: contractor must use Miami‑Dade NOA‑approved materials and installation methods for hurricane performance.  
- Florida contractor license (check DBPR) and local business tax receipt.  
- Manufacturer certifications (e.g., GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT, etc.) — means trained to install that product’s wind/impact systems.  
- Adequate insurance: General liability + workers’ comp. Ask for certificates naming you as additional insured during work if requested.  
- Experience with hurricane‑rated systems (metal standing seam, properly installed concrete/terracotta tile, or Class‑4 impact shingles with appropriate attachments).  
- Strong local references and plenty of recent Miami area jobs.

What to verify / ask every contractor
- Can you provide your Florida license number, proof of insurance, and local references?  
- Do you use Miami‑Dade NOA‑approved products and installers? Show documentation.  
- Will you pull permits and schedule inspections? (They should.)  
- What wind‑uplift rating and fastening schedule will you use? Ask for the wind‑uplift calculation and fastening pattern.  
- What warranties come with the roof (manufacturer vs workmanship) and are warranties transferable?  
- Who will handle the insurance claim if applicable? Will you meet the adjuster?  
- Timeline, payment schedule, and written scope specifying materials, underlayment, deck attachments, flashing, and vents.

Red flags
- Contractor asks for large up‑front cash payment or only accepts cash.  
- No local references or inability/unwillingness to show license/insurance.  
- Vague scope, no permit work, or unwillingness to provide written estimate with details.  
- Extremely low bid far below others (could mean shortcuts or unlicensed work).

Where to check credentials and reviews
- Florida DBPR contractor search (verify license status).  
- Miami‑Dade County Product Control / NOA database (confirm product approvals).  
- BBB, Google Reviews, Yelp, local neighborhood groups for references.  
- Manufacturer locator pages (to find certified installers).

Materials & installation items to expect for hurricane‑rated replacement
- Properly fastened roof deck and hurricane straps/ties at truss/rafter connections.  
- Secondary water barrier (ice/water isn't relevant in FL; look for high‑quality underlayment/peel‑and‑stick or manufacturer‑approved systems).  
- Correct flashing, sealed penetrations, and continuous ridge/soffit ventilation per manufacturer specs.  
- Impact‑rated (Class 4) products or tested metal/tile systems with proper fastening.

If you want, I can:
- Recommend a short list of well‑reviewed Miami firms if you give your ZIP code or neighborhood (I’ll describe how to vet each).  
- Review written estimates you’ve received and point out omissions or concerns.  
Tell me your ZIP code or paste up to three company names/estimates and I’ll help you evaluate them.
